379	 * Name: setup_timer
380	 *
381	 * Description:
382	 *   Setup LEDC timer frequency and reload.
383	 *
384	 * Input Parameters:
385	 *   priv - A reference to the LEDC timer state structure
386	 *
387	 * Returned Value:
388	 *   None
389	 *
390	 ****************************************************************************/
391	
392	static void setup_timer(struct esp32s3_ledc_s *priv)
393	{
394	  irqstate_t flags;
395	  uint32_t regval;
396	  uint32_t reload;
397	  float prescaler;
398	  uint32_t integral_prescaler;
399	  uint32_t fractional_prescaler;
400	  uint8_t shift;
401	  uint64_t pwmclk = LEDC_CLK_APB_FREQ;
402	
403	  /* Determine the using clock source and set pwmclk */
404	
405	  switch (clk_src)
406	  {
407	  case LEDC_CLK_RES_APB:
408	
409	    /* use APB clock */
410	
411	    pwmclk = LEDC_CLK_APB_FREQ;
412	    break;
413	
414	  case LEDC_CLK_RES_RC_FAST:
415	
416	    /* use RC_FAST clock */
417	
418	    pwmclk = LEDC_CLK_RC_FAST_FREQ;
419	    break;
420	
421	  case LEDC_CLK_RES_XTAL:
422	
423	    /* use XTAL clock */
424	
425	    pwmclk = LEDC_CLK_XTAL_FREQ;
426	    break;
427	
428	  default:
429	    pwmerr("Invalid clock source or no clock has been inited !");
430	    break;
431	  }
432	
433	  /* Reset timer */
434	
435	  SET_TIMER_BITS(priv, LEDC_TIMER0_CONF_REG, LEDC_TIMER0_RST);
436	
437	  /* Calculate optimal values for the timer prescaler and for the timer
438	   * modulo register.  If 'frequency' is the desired frequency, then
439	   *
440	   *   tpmclk = pwmclk / presc
441	   *   frequency = tpmclk / reload
442	   *
443	   * ==>
444	   *
445	   *   reload = pwmclk / presc / frequency
446	   *
447	   * In ESP32S3, there are 3 clock resources for PWM:
448	   *
449	   *   1. APB clock (80 MHz)
450	   *   2. RC_FAST_CLK (17.5 MHz)
451	   *   3. XTAL_CLK (40 MHZ)
452	   *
453	   * We mostly use APB clock generally.
454	   *
455	   * There are many solutions to this, but the best solution will be the one
456	   * that has the largest reload value and the smallest prescaler value.
457	   * That is the solution that should give us the most accuracy in the timer
458	   * control.  Subject to:
459	   *
460	   *   2 <= presc  <= 2^14(16384)
461	   *   1 <= clkdiv <= 2^10
462	   *
463	   * clkdiv has 10-bit integral precision and 8-bit fractional precision, so
464	   * clkdiv = pwmclk / 16384 / frequency would be optimal.
465	   *
466	   * Example:
467	   *
468	   *  pwmclk    = 80 MHz
469	   *  frequency = 100 Hz
470	   *
471	   *  presc     = 80,000,000 * 256 / 16,384 / 100
472	   *            = 12,500
473	   *  timclk    = 80,000,000 / (12,500 / 256)
474	   *            = 1,638,400
475	   *  counter   = 1,638,400 / 100
476	   *            = 16,384
477	   *            = 2^14
478	   *  shift     = 14
479	   */
480	
481	  /* Search the maximum value of timer reload value */
482	
483	  for (reload = LEDC_RELOAD_MAX , shift = LEDC_RELOAD_MAX_BIT_LEN;
484	       reload > 1;
485	       reload = (reload >> 1), shift -= 1)
486	      {
487	        if (reload * priv->frequency <= pwmclk)
488	        {
489	          break;
490	        }
491	  }
492	
493	  /* Caculate the prescaler */
494	
495	  prescaler = (float)pwmclk / priv->frequency / reload;
496	
497	  /* Get the integral part */
498	
499	  integral_prescaler = (uint32_t) prescaler;
500	
501	  /* Get the fractional part. To write to the registers, value need to be
502	  * multiply by 256
503	  */
504	
505	  fractional_prescaler = (uint32_t)((prescaler - integral_prescaler) * 256);
506	
507	  /* Prevent prescaler goto 0. In esp32 series, prescaler == 1 means
508	  * clock signal goes pass-through
509	  */
510	
511	  if (integral_prescaler == 0) integral_prescaler = 1;
512	
513	  pwminfo("PWM timer%" PRIu8 " frequency=%0.4f reload=%" PRIu32 " shift=%"
514	          PRIu32 " prescaler=%0.4f\n",
515	          priv->num, (float)pwmclk / reload / ((float)prescaler),
516	          reload, shift, (float)prescaler);
517	
518	  /* Store reload for channel duty */
519	
520	  priv->reload = reload;
521	
522	  flags = enter_critical_section();
523	
524	  /* Set timer clock divide and reload */
525	
526	  regval = (shift << LEDC_TIMER0_DUTY_RES_S) |
527	           (fractional_prescaler << LEDC_CLK_DIV_TIMER0_S) |
528	           (integral_prescaler << LEDC_CLK_DIV_TIMER0_S << 8);
529	  SET_TIMER_REG(priv, LEDC_TIMER0_CONF_REG, regval);
530	
531	  /* Update clock divide and reload to hardware */
532	
533	  SET_TIMER_BITS(priv, LEDC_TIMER0_CONF_REG, LEDC_TIMER0_PARA_UP);
534	
535	  leave_critical_section(flags);
536	}

## Context

The file `packages/demos/esp_test/esp_test_main.c` contains stub PWM lower-half callback functions (`my_pwm_setup`, `my_pwm_shutdown`, `my_pwm_start`, `my_pwm_stop`, `my_pwm_ioctl`) that only print messages and return OK. struct my_pwm_priv_s {
    struct pwm_lowerhalf_s dev;  /* Must be first for casting */
    int timer;                   /* LEDC timer number */
    int channel;                 /* LEDC channel number */
    int gpio;                    /* GPIO pin number */

};
